newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rio state may ask cenbank to keep running Banerj.
newsitem.headline: Rio state may ask cenbank to keep running Banerj.

text.p: Rio de Janeiro state government may ask Brazil's Central Bank to continue running state bank Banco Banerj under its special administration program which ends in June, said a spokesman for the state's Planning office.

Rio is seeking more time to privatize the bank. The sell-off hinges on Senate approval of a 2.9 billion real loan from federal bank Caixa Economica Federal (CEF) to finance necessary adjustments prior to the bank's sale, he said.
If Banerj is not privatized by June and the extension is not granted, the bank may be liquidated.
The spokesman also said Rio de Janeiro Planning Secretary Marco Aurelio Alencar would hold talks with foreign banks to drum up interest in Banerj's privatization.
Alencar told reporters last week that HSBC Holdings Plc, which took over retail bank Banco Bamerindus in late March, was interested in Banerj.
Rio de Janeiro attempted to privatize Banerj last year, but a court halted the bank's sell-off.

However, analysts also noted that that auction had not drawn much interest. Only Brazil's two largest private banks -- Bradesco and Banco Itau -- out of eight pre-qualified investors signed up for the auction.
To entice more investors, Rio de Janeiro state government is revising the privatization rules governing the Banerj sale, and new tender documents are expected.
No date has been set for the release of the new tender details.
